messages.author: 7f4225fd2234920f
messages.subject: distsamp: Error in optim
parts:
Hi -
I'm using the distsamp function but keep running into the same error:

Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :
initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

I've already standardized my covariates and provided starting values,
but nothing seems to help. My data are pretty sparse, so I'm not sure
if that is part of the problem. I attached some of the code below as
well a summary of the unmarked frame. Maybe I'm just missing
something obvious? Any suggestions you have would be much appreciated!

Thanks,
Erin

> umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat2), siteCovs=Covariates[,2:4], survey="line", tlength = 1000,
+ dist.breaks=db, unitsIn="m")
> summary(umf)

120 sites
Maximum number of distance classes per site: 5
Mean number of distance classes per site: 5
Sites with at least one detection: 80

Tabulation of y observations:
0 1 2 3 <NA>
481 99 17 3 0

Site-level covariates:
District DistRoad DistORoad
RMD:60 Min. :-1.188e+00 Min. :-1.534e+00
TMD:60 1st Qu.:-7.960e-01 1st Qu.:-8.788e-01
Median :-3.895e-01 Median :-1.237e-01
Mean : 1.667e-11 Mean :-2.500e-11
3rd Qu.: 6.353e-01 3rd Qu.: 8.256e-01
Max. : 2.483e+00 Max. : 2.607e+00

Both of these models give me the same "Error in optim" message,
regardless of what I provide as starting values:

> Road.District <- distsamp(~DistRoad ~District, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", starts=c(0,0,0,0))
> null <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ 1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", starts=c(-1,1))

 We had this error last week in an analysis due to ill-treatment of missing values. It doesn't look like you have any though.

regards
andy

parts:
hi Erin,
 I'm posting this on the list for general information , and also for Richard to see in case he has an idea on whats up.
 
I ran your model in the more general function "gdistsamp" which allows for Robust Design type data (for open populations)  and it seems to work ok.  See below. gdistsamp() fill handle normal distance sampling if you say numPrimary=1.
 
 I used the estimates as starting values in distsamp() and it still doesn't work.....
 
 So try using gdistsamp() for now until we figure out why distsamp() doesn't work.
 
regards
andy
 
 
# Organize data
umf <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = yDat2, survey="line", unitsIn="m",
    dist.breaks=db, tlength=rep(1000, 120), numPrimary=1)
summary(umf)
# Fit the model
m1 <- gdistsamp(~1, ~1, ~1, umf, output="density")
summary(m1)
 
> m1 <- gdistsamp(~1, ~1, ~1, umf, output="density")

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] distsamp: Error in optim
parts:
hi Erin,
 got it -- you need to specify tlength  = rep(1000,120)  (i.e., one element for each transect). It works then:
 
regards
andy
 
umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat2), siteCovs=Covariates[,2:4], survey="line", tlength = rep( 1000,120),
       dist.breaks=db, unitsIn="m")

null <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ 1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha",starts=c(-.3,2))
 
> null <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ 1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha",starts=c(-.3,2))
